analysisTemplates.description: App-specific custom Argo Rollouts AnalysisTemplates, referenced by name from rollout.steps or rollout.canaryAnalysis. Not rendered as a Rollout - referenced only.

appName.description: This application's name. Used as the Helm release name's basis, the default ServiceAccount name, and the default databaseName for a PostgreSQL component. A DNS-1123 label: lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, must start and end with an alphanumeric.

appType.description: app runs a workload (Rollout); infra provisions components/environments only (naming-conventions.md's existing distinction).

attachedResourceApiVersion.description: The apiVersion group used to look up component/SLO XRs by componentKinds. Update here, not per-template, if the group ever changes.

autoscaling.description: HorizontalPodAutoscaler settings for the main workload.

cluster.description: Which cluster this release runs on. Not in the original service-catalog design's schema block - the chart needs it to know its own identity (e.g. to compare against devClusterName below), and the ApplicationEnvironment composition that commits this file already knows it.

componentKinds.description: Deliberate lookup map exception: component type string -> XR kind. Not every listed kind has a real XRD yet.

components.description: Attached-tier component instances (Redis, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, ...). Each entry's spec is validated against that component's own XRD schema by the compiled schema (airframe_schema.compiled_schema()), not by this file directly - see tools/airframe-validate.

configMaps.description: ConfigMaps mounted or projected as env vars into the main workload.

cronJobs.description: Scheduled batch tasks (nightly cleanup, report generation, ...). Share env/secrets/configMaps/volumes with the main container automatically.

devClusterName.description: The name of this fleet's dev cluster, compared against `cluster` to decide dev-vs-upper behavior (e.g. secretsScope). Not the literal cluster context name in every case - see docs/admin - override only if a fleet's dev cluster is ever named something other than kind-dev.

env.description: Container environment variables for the main workload.

envName.description: The environment name (dev, staging, prod, or a PR number). Named envName, not env, because env is already this schema's top-level container env-var list - a same-named field would collide in one flat values map.

extraManifests.description: Last-resort escape hatch - a raw list of arbitrary Kubernetes objects, rendered as-is, no labels stamped.

httpRoute.description: Gateway API HTTPRoute, first-class alongside classic ingress. This platform's convention: <app>.<cluster-or-env-qualifier>.kiac.local.

ingress.description: Classic Ingress. Gateway API (httpRoute below) is the mechanism most new callers actually want on this fleet's real clusters.

jobs.description: One-off batch tasks - the common 'run a DB migration before the new Rollout comes up' pattern. Same image/env/secrets/configMaps/volumes defaulting as cronJobs.

namespace.description: Extra labels/annotations stamped on this release's own Namespace object.

networkPolicy.description: Traffic policy for the main workload's namespace.

notifications.description: AI-triage diagnosis notifications, threaded into the RolloutWatch XR this chart renders unconditionally.

platformSecretStore.description: Unused since the release-tracking hook Jobs and their relay-token ExternalSecret were removed (glidepath ADR-0021 phase 3b); kept so existing env files that set it still validate.

podDisruptionBudget.description: Set at most one of minAvailable/maxUnavailable.

release.description: Machine-owned: written by the release pipeline (Glidepath) into the release file, never by hand in a human-owned env file. Takes precedence over the deprecated rollout.image. No workload renders (Rollout/Service/ServiceMonitor) until both release.image fields are set.

releaseTracking.description: Opaque escape hatch, deliberately excluded from the strictness rule: written by glidepath's open-release-pr.yaml, never hand-authored. Null when this env hasn't gone through a release pipeline yet. Only releaseId and appNamespace are read (glidepath ADR-0021): releaseId is rendered onto the Rollout as the hangar.io/release-id annotation, with a hangar.io/release-tracked label, so the Argo Rollouts notifications engine can report the release; appNamespace is the dev-cluster namespace of the release record. Older release files also carry relayUrl, relayHostAliasIP, configJsonB64 and other fields for the removed hook Jobs; they are ignored. Setting releaseTracking on a release with no Rollout fails the render.

rollout.description: The Argo Rollout workload. Set to null for an infra-type release with no custom workload (a standalone component-only env).

secrets.description: Secrets, aggregated into one app-secrets Secret via ExternalSecret/ClusterSecretStore, consumed by the main container.

serviceAccount.description: Kubernetes ServiceAccount for every workload this chart renders.

serviceMonitor.description: Prometheus scraping of the main workload's first rollout.ports entry, via kube-prometheus-stack.

slos.description: Rendered into the SLO XRD (xrds/slo.yaml), which wraps Sloth. No window/burn-rate fields here - Sloth computes those from just objective.

volumes.description: PVC-backed volumes for the main workload.

reasons.meaning: (attach mode) the client is registered on the server and {name}-oauth-credentials carries the secret the server actually holds - created fresh, confirmed unchanged, or adopted from the server when the Secret had been lost or drifted (the message says which; adoption also raises a Warning event).

(attach mode) the live CreateClient/GetClient call to the Dex server's gRPC Admin API failed (server unreachable, or a real error), or the client exists on the server without a secret this XR can use. A previously observed Secret is kept as it was, never pruned.
(server mode) the Dex Deployment has at least one available replica.
(server mode) the Dex Deployment has not reported an available replica yet.

dex.summary: attach mode: a confidential OAuth2 client on an existing shared Dex server, for machine-to-machine client_credentials auth. server mode (no outputs below apply): the shared OIDC server itself.

verify.check: The Dex XR's ComponentReady condition has reason DexAttachReady (attach) or DexServerReady (server).
Secret {name}-oauth-credentials exists in the app namespace with non-empty client-id and client-secret keys.

POST {tokenUrl} with grant_type=client_credentials and the client-id/client-secret from the Secret returns a real access_token whose signing key is published at {jwksUrl} (reached through kubectl port-forward to the Dex server's Service).
The Dex server's {name} Service answers GET /dex/.well-known/openid-configuration with 200 on 5556 (through kubectl port-forward).

reasons.meaning: The MongoDBCommunity replica set reports phase Running.
The MongoDBCommunity replica set reports phase Failed - a real problem, not just startup. Check its own status.message.

The replica set has not been observed yet (just created).

uri.description: A full mongodb:// connection string, credentials and all replica set members included. The key itself contains a literal dot - it is one flat Secret key, "connectionString.standard", not a nested field.

uriSrv.description: The same connection string, using mongodb+srv:// DNS seedlist discovery instead of listing every member.

sources.note: The MongoDB Kubernetes operator writes each user's connection strings into the Secret named by users[].connectionStringSecretName.
The operator creates the headless <name>-svc Service for the replica set's StatefulSet.

mongodb.summary: A dedicated MongoDB replica set, one per application environment.

verify.check: The MongoDB XR's ComponentReady condition has reason MongoDBReady.

reasons.meaning: The CNPG Cluster's own Ready condition is True.

The Cluster has not been observed yet (just created).

uri.description: A full postgres:// connection string, credentials included.

sources.note: CloudNativePG creates <Cluster>-app (owner role, generated password, uri, jdbc-uri) from bootstrap.initdb.

reasons.meaning: (attach mode) The User and Permission are provisioned on the shared broker.

reasons.meaning: The wrapped Bitnami chart reports deployed.

host.description: The master Service's in-cluster DNS name.

password.description: The Crossplane-composed connection Secret (writeConnectionSecretToRef), not the raw Bitnami chart Secret (which also exists, named `{name}`, key `redis-password` - the connection Secret copies the same value here so every component type has one canonical `<name>-connection` output surface).

url.description: host:port only, no credentials embedded (auth.enabled is true on this component, so a connection still needs the password output supplied separately - e.g. as its own env var).

ApplicationEnvironment.agentSummary: Adds a deploy environment (e.g. staging, prod) on a target cluster for an app that's already been onboarded.

AwsEcsTarget.agentSummary: Stand up the AWS infrastructure a container deploys into on ECS Fargate (cluster, task definition, service, execution role and a small public network) - disposable, for an app's deploy.target: aws-ecs.

AwsLambdaTarget.agentSummary: Stand up the AWS infrastructure a container-image Lambda function deploys into (ECR repository, execution role, function, public URL) - disposable, for a LambdaFunction app's deploy.target: aws-lambda.

AzureContainerAppTarget.agentSummary: Stand up the Azure infrastructure a container deploys into on Container Apps (resource group, environment, app with public ingress) - disposable, for an app's deploy.target: azure-container-apps.

AzureFunction.agentSummary: Onboard a new Azure Functions app (container image) - creates its source repo with an HTTP function and CI/CD that deploys to an existing Container App.

Dex.agentSummary: A shared Dex OIDC server (mode: server) or a machine-to-machine OAuth2 client on an existing one (mode: attach).

GoApplication.agentSummary: Onboard a new Go service - creates its source repo (with boilerplate) and an empty GitOps deploy repo, then wires up CI/CD.

InfraService.agentSummary: Provisions standalone shared infrastructure (e.g. a cache or datastore another app depends on) - just an empty GitOps deploy repo, no application source code.

LambdaFunction.agentSummary: Onboard a new AWS Lambda function (container image) - creates its source repo with a handler and CI/CD that deploys to an existing function.

MongoDB.agentSummary: A dedicated MongoDB replica set (MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes' MongoDBCommunity CRD), one per application environment.

NodeJSApplication.agentSummary: Onboard a new Node.js service - creates its source repo (with boilerplate) and an empty GitOps deploy repo, then wires up CI/CD.

PostgreSQL.agentSummary: A dedicated PostgreSQL database (CloudNativePG), one per application environment.

PythonApplication.agentSummary: Onboard a new Python service - creates its source repo (with boilerplate) and an empty GitOps deploy repo, then wires up CI/CD.

RabbitMQ.agentSummary: A shared RabbitMQ broker (mode: broker) or a scoped user/permission on an existing one (mode: attach).

Redis.agentSummary: A Redis cache or shared-counter store, dedicated to one application environment.

RolloutWatch.agentSummary: Watches an app's Argo Rollout and runs AI-triage diagnosis on a failed canary.

SLO.agentSummary: Declares a service-level objective, rendered into Sloth for multi-window burn-rate alerting.

SecretStore.agentSummary: Creates or extends this app's Infisical-backed secret store (project, identity, ClusterSecretStore) for one cluster.

SpringBootApplication.agentSummary: Onboard a new Java/Spring Boot service - creates its source repo (with boilerplate) and an empty GitOps deploy repo, then wires up CI/CD.

TektonCICD.agentSummary: Wires a new app repo into the shared Tekton/PaC CI/CD pipeline and tenant onboarding.
